newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian economic czar defends CEPA investment plan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian economic czar defends CEPA investment plan.

text.p: Malaysia's Economic Adviser to the Government on Wednesday slammed critics of the state's overseas business deals, saying a planned involvement in Hong Kong's CEPA Ltd was among ventures needed by Malaysia.

"If the venture is viable, what's wrong with that? We (the government) are not stupid to be used by companies," Daim Zainuddin, often regarded as czar of Malaysia's economic reformation, was quoted as saying by the Bernama news agency.

Daim, a former finance minister, was commenting on remarks by government parliamentarian Ruhanie Ahmad on Tuesday that the government should be careful before allowing state funds to be used to finance the overseas projects of Malaysian firms.
Ruhanie had in parliament singled out a plan by Malaysian infrastructure developer and power company YTL Corp Bhd to buy over Hong Kong's Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA).
The $2.6 billion bid by YTL fell through on Tuesday after the Malaysian company said that CEPA's controlling shareholder, tycoon Gordon Wu, would not commit "irrevocably" to the deal.
YTL said on Tuesday that state investment company Khazanah Nasional had agreed to make an equity investment of $1 billion in the aborted deal.
Daim said that Khazanah would have done a detailed study before granting a loan to YTL.
Although Khazanah would have protected itself with various conditions for the loan, it could have even bought shares in CEPA at a lower price from YTL, said Daim.
Daim said Malaysia should not be concerned about investing in Hong Kong although the British territory would revert to Chinese rule next year.
"We are alreading investing in China and many other countries. If we want to be big, we must learn to start going overseas in a big way now," he said.
